1.note: The author is using the words **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

David is using the term **Behold** to focus Nathan’s attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Listen]
Here, **cedars** represent cedar wood. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in a house built of cedar wood]

David is not referring to window decorations. Israelites characteristically referred to the individual pieces of cloth that they sewed together to make tents as **curtains**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [is under tent-curtains] or [is in a tent]

2.q: כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽ⁠לְבָבְ⁠ךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֑ה כִּ֥י הָ⁠אֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּֽ⁠ךְ
2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [God is with you, so do all that is in your heart]
Here, the **heart** represents a person’s desires. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All that you desire to do]
See how you translated the expression “would be with me” in 4:10. Alternate translation: [God will help you]

3.note: The author is using the words **But it happened** to introduce a new development in this episode. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new development.

When the author says that **the word of God was to Nathan**, he is using a common expression to mean that God spoke a message to Nathan. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that God spoke a message to Nathan]

4.q: לֵ֤ךְ וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֣יד עַבְדִּ֔⁠י כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֥א אַתָּ֛ה תִּבְנֶה־לִּ֥⁠י הַ⁠בַּ֖יִת לָ⁠שָֽׁבֶת
4.note: See the discussion in the Introduction to this chapter of how you might use punctuation or some other convention of your language to indicate the second-level, third-level, and fourth-level quotations in Yahweh’s message to Nathan in verses 4–14. That discussion also suggests that, alternatively, you could translate these verses in such a way that there are not quotations within quotations. The UST models one way to do that.

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **You** separately, even though the verbal phrase translated as **you shall not build** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that David is wanting to do something that he has never asked the Israelites to do for him. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [No, you shall not build]

Yahweh is speaking here as if David wants to build him a physical **house** as his **dwelling**. He is actually speaking of a temple where he would be present with his people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a temple where I will be present]

5.note: Here the word **For** provides not a reason but an explanation. Alternate translation: [After all]

Yahweh is speaking as if a temple were actually a physical **house** in which he might live. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in a temple]
Yahweh is using the term **day** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [since the time]

Yahweh is marking travel for change in elevation as he refers to how he brought the people of Israel out of slavery in Egypt and into the land of Canaan. Translate this the same way you have been translating similar expressions. Alternate translation: [when I brought the people of Israel here]

Yahweh is using a common expression of this culture not to mean that he has moved from one **tent** to another but that he has moved from one place to another in the same tent. He is referring to how he accompanied the Israelites on their journey from Egypt to Canaan. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but I have moved from one place to another in a tent]

Yahweh is describing how that same tent became a fixed sanctuary for him in various places in the land of Canaan. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. The UST models one way to do that.

6.q: הֲ⁠דָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתִי לִ⁠רְע֥וֹת אֶת־עַמִּ֖⁠י לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר לָ֛⁠מָּה לֹא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖⁠י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים
6.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize to David that he never asked any of Israel’s leaders to build him a temple. As he makes this point, he includes a shorter question whose form he could have used, but did not use, to emphasize to the Israelite leaders that they should have built a temple for him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for these purposes, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [I did not speak a word with one of the scepters of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, ‘You should have built a house of cedars for me!’]

Yahweh is using the term **word** to represent what he might have said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [did I give a command to]

Here, **scepters** represents “leaders,” since leaders held scepters as an emblem of their office. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [any of the leaders of Israel]

ere, Yahweh is speaking as if each of these leaders was a **shepherd** and as if his **people Israel** were sheep. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to guide]

The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh would be asking why the Israelites had not done something, even though he would be addressing **one of the scepters of Israel**, that is, an Israelite leader. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated the same expression in [17:1](ta:17). Alternate translation: [a temple built from cedar wood]

7.note: **And now** was an expression that speakers in this culture commonly used to introduce their main topic. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, here and in verses 23, 26, and 27. You could also use plain language.

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I took** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize his personal role in the activity he describes. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I personally took you]

Yahweh is referring to the way a shepherd works in a **pasture** and walks behind a **flock** to represent the work of a shepherd generally. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from being a shepherd]

8.note: See how you translated the expression “God {is} with you” in 17:2. Alternate translation: [And I have helped you]

Yahweh is speaking as if he had physically **cut off** David’s enemies, as if they had been a branch he wanted to remove from a tree. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I have destroyed]

Here, **from your face** means “in front of you,” with the implication that these enemies were confronting David and opposing him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before you] or [who opposed you]

Here, a person’s **name** represents his reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a reputation for you like the reputation of]

Yahweh is using the adjective **great** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the great leaders]

9.q: וּ⁠נְטַעְתִּ֨י⁠הוּ֙ וְ⁠שָׁכַ֣ן תַּחְתָּ֔י⁠ו וְ⁠לֹ֥א יִרְגַּ֖ז & לְ⁠בַלֹּת֔⁠וֹ
9.note: In this verse, the words **him** and **he** are singular in form, but they refer to all the Israelites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural forms of these words. Alternate translation: [and I will plant them that they may dwell in their place, and they will not tremble … to afflict them]

Yahweh is speaking here as if he would physically **plant** the Israelites, as if they were a tree or some other plant. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will make them secure]

Yahweh is using a common expression of this culture that means “that the Israelites may live on the ground that is under them.” Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. You could also use plain language. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression “we will stand under us” in 1 Samuel 14:9. Alternate translation: [that the Israelites may live in that place]

Here, to **tremble** represents being afraid. It refers to trembling with fear. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and he will not be afraid] or [and they will not be afraid]
See how you translated the similar expression “sons of valor” in 5:18. Alternate translation: [And wicked people]

The phrase **at first** refers to an earlier time. If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **first**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use or in some other way that would be clear in your language. Alternate translation: [as formerly]

10.note: Yahweh is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and during the time when]

In making an official declaration, Yahweh is speaking about himself formally in the third person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [that I, Yahweh, will build]
See how you translated the expression “the house of Saul” in 12:29. Alternate translation: [a royal dynasty]

11.note: Yahweh is using **When your days are full** as a common expression of this culture to mean “when you have lived your whole life.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [When you have lived your whole life]

Yahweh is referring to death in a polite way. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [and you pass away as your fathers have] or [and it is time for you to join your fathers in death]
Yahweh is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your ancestors]

Yahweh is speaking as if he will physically **raise up** one of David’s descendants to a high location. He means that he will make him become the next king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then I will make reign as king after you]

Yahweh is speaking of David’s descendant as if he were a **seed** and as if David were a plant that had produced it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [one of your offspring]

12.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **he will build** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he is making a promise to David. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I promise that he will build]
See how you translated the term :house” in 17:4. Alternate translation: [a temple]

Here, **throne** represents the authority to rule as king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language, here and in verse 14. Alternate translation: [his reign as king]

Here, the expression **to forever** means “to indefinite futurity,” that is, “for as long into the future as anyone can imagine.” Yahweh does not mean that this son of David will never die. He means that no one will ever replace him as king, as David replaced Saul. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers, here and in verse 14. The UST models one way to do that.

13.q: אֲנִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶה־לּ֣⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָ֔ב וְ⁠ה֖וּא יִֽהְיֶה־לִּ֣⁠י לְ⁠בֵ֑ן
13.note: Yahweh is stating the pronouns **I** and **he** separately, even though the verbs translated as **I will be** and **he will be** already include those meanings. He is doing that because he is identifying the complementary roles that he and David’s son will have. If a speaker of your language would use explicit pronouns for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that meaning here. Alternate translation: [For my part, I will be a father to him, and for his part, he will be a son to me]

13.q: אֲנִי֙ אֶֽהְיֶה־לּ֣⁠וֹ לְ⁠אָ֔ב וְ⁠ה֖וּא יִֽהְיֶה־לִּ֣⁠י לְ⁠בֵ֑ן
13.note: Yahweh is speaking here as if he and David’s descendant would actually be **father** and **son**. He means that he will treat David’s descendant the way a father treats a son. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will treat him the way a father treats his son]

13.q: וְ⁠חַסְדִּ⁠י֙ לֹא־אָסִ֣יר מֵֽ⁠עִמּ֔⁠וֹ כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲסִיר֔וֹתִי מֵ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה לְ⁠פָנֶֽי⁠ךָ
13.note: Yahweh is speaking of his **covenant faithfulness** as if it were an object that he could **turn away** from someone. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will not stop treating him with covenant faithfulness as I stopped treating him with it who was to your face]
As the parallel in 2 Samuel 7:15 makes clear, Yahweh is referring to Saul. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from Saul, who was to your face]

Here, **face** represents what is before a person in time, that is, prior to the perron’s current situation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [was before you] or [who was king before you were]

14.note: This could mean: (1) that Yahweh is speaking as if he will appoint David’s son to be an important official in a royal palace where he reigns as king. Alternate translation: [And I will make him a great ruler under my authority] or (2) that Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel as if they were his **house**, that is, his household. In that case, **in my house and in my kingdom** would mean “in the kingdom that consists of my house,” that is, “my Israelite kingdom.” Alternate translation: [And I will make him reign over my Israelite kingdom]

The expression **will be established** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and I will establish his throne]

15.q: כְּ⁠כֹל֙ הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֔לֶּה וּ⁠כְ⁠כֹ֖ל הֶ⁠חָז֣וֹן הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה
15.note: Together, the terms **words** and **vision** express a single idea. The term **vision** tells how Yahweh conveyed these **words** to David. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [According to all of these words that Yahweh had spoken to him in a vision]

15.q: כְּ⁠כֹל֙ הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֔לֶּה וּ⁠כְ⁠כֹ֖ל הֶ⁠חָז֣וֹן הַ⁠זֶּ֑ה
15.note: Here, **words** represents what Yahweh said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [According to all of these things that Yahweh had said to him in a vision]

16.note: Here, **face** represents “presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of Yahweh]

16.q: מִֽי־אֲנִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ וּ⁠מִ֣י בֵיתִ֔⁠י כִּ֥י הֲבִיאֹתַ֖⁠נִי עַד־הֲלֹֽם
16.note: David is using the question form to express his humility and amazement at what God has done for him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [I am not so significant, my Lord Yahweh, and neither is my house, that you should have brought me to here!]
By **my house**, David probably means his “father’s house,” that is, the extended family from which he comes. Alternate translation: [my family]

he implication is that **here** means being the king of Israel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [that you have made me the king of Israel]

17.note: David is using **this was small in your eyes** as a common expression of his culture to mean “you considered this to be insignificant.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you considered this a small thing]

David is speaking of himself in the third person as **your servant** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person, here and in the rest of this chapter. Alternate translation: [my house]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So **the house of your servant** figuratively means all the people who would descend from David. Alternate translation: [my descendants]

David is using **a man {of} ascent** as a common expression of his culture to mean a powerful and important person. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as if I were a high-ranking man] or [as if I were a noble]

18.q: מַה־יּוֹסִ֨יף ע֥וֹד דָּוִ֛יד אֵלֶ֖י⁠ךָ לְ⁠כָב֣וֹד אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑⁠ךָ
18.note: David is using the question form to express that he is too overwhelmed to say anything more. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There is nothing more for David to say to you about honoring your servant!]

18.q: מַה־יּוֹסִ֨יף ע֥וֹד דָּוִ֛יד אֵלֶ֖י⁠ךָ לְ⁠כָב֣וֹד אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑⁠ךָ
18.note: David is speaking of himself in the third person as **David** and **your servant** to show humility. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in a humble form in the first person. Alternate translation: [What more can I say to you about honoring me?] or [There is nothing more for me to say to you about honoring me!]

David is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you know** already includes this meaning. He is doing that in order to contrast Yahweh’s knowledge of what he is thinking and feeling with his own inability to say anything further. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [But for your part, you know your servant] or [But for your part, you know me]

The implication of Yahweh knowing David is that he knows what David would say if he were able to say anything further. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [you know what I, your servant, would say further if I could]

19.note: Here, the **heart** represents a person’s desires. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and according to your desire] or [and because you wanted to]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **greatness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all these great things]

In this context, the verb form **to make {me} know** does not describe the purpose of the preceding action, **you have done all of this greatness**. Instead, it describes an accompanying action. Use an appropriate verbal form in your language to convey this meaning. Alternate translation: [and you have made me know]

David is using the plural **greatnesses** where he could have used the singular form. This suggests that he is using the plural form to emphasize how very great Yahweh’s promises to him are. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the singular and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [all of these very great things]

20.note: Recall how you have decided to translate poetic pairs of statements that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [there is none like you, indeed, there is no God except you]
If it would appear in your language that David was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [and you are the only God]

It might seem that in this context, the expression **with our ears** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could leave it out. Alternate translation: [in all that we have heard]

21.note: David is using the question form for emphasis. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And there is no other nation like your people Israel … from Egypt!]
In certain contexts, Hebrew speakers would use forms of the word “go” to mean “take action.” Alternate translation: [took action to redeem]

The expression **feared** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a great name that people would respect]
See how you translated the word “name” in 16:29. Alternate translation: [a great reputation that people would respect]

Here, **from the face of** means “in front of,” with the implication that Yahweh did these fearsome things to defeat the enemies who were confronting the Israelites and opposing them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of] or [that opposed]

23.note: See how you translated the expression “And now” in 17:7.

David is using the term **word** to represent what God said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the things that you have said]
See how you translated the term “house” in 17:10. Alternate translation: [concerning your servant and concerning his dynasty] or [concerning me and my dynasty]
Recall how you have decided to translate poetic pairs of statements that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [may it be confirmed to forever, yes, do just as you have spoken]

The expression **were born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language, here and at the start of the next verse. Alternate translation: [may you confirm it]

24.note: The second wish that David expresses here may describe the purpose for the first wish that he expresses. Alternate translation: [And may you confirm it so that your name will be great to forever]
Here, **name** represents “reputation.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [your reputation]

24.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְ⁠יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
24.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [so that people will say that you, Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, are God to Israel]

The expression **be established** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and may you establish the house of David your servant]
See how you translated the term “house” in the previous verse. Alternate translation: [the dynasty of David your servant] or [my dynasty]

This could mean: (1) that David is using one part of Yahweh, his **face**, to mean all of him in the act of maintaining the rule of David and his descendants. The idea is that Yahweh would be watching them and protecting them. Alternate translation: [as you maintain it]; (2) that David is using Yahweh’s **face** to represent his presence. Alternate translation: [in your presence]

25.note: Here the word **For** provides not a reason but an explanation. Alternate translation: [After all]

David is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you have uncovered** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize God’s personal role in the activity he describes. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you, my God, have personally uncovered the ear of your servant]

David is using a common expression, **you have uncovered the ear**, that described one person telling something to another person. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have told this to your servant] or [you have told this to me]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [saying that you are going to build a house for him] or [saying that you are going to establish a dynasty for me]

The parallel passage in 2 Samuel 7:27 reads “your servant has found his heart to pray,” with the “heart” representing “courage.” The term “heart” may have dropped out here in the process of copying, or the author may be leaving it to be understood. You can supply this word if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [your servant has found his heart to pray] or [I have found the courage to pray]

David is using one part of Yahweh, his **face**, to mean all of him in the act of listening to his prayer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation, as in 2 Samuel 7:27: [to you]

26.note: It might seem that the expression **you {are} he, God** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [you are God]
